triples.subject: Ivan
triples.quote: By the way, let us say a word or two of Ivan’s feeling to his brother Dmitri.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: By the way, let us say a word or two of Ivan’s feeling to his brother Dmitri.

triples.subject: Katerina Ivanovna
triples.quote: Ivan looked with indignation on Katerina Ivanovna’s love for his brother.

triples.subject: Alyosha
triples.quote: ascribed his opinion only to his exaggerated brotherly feeling and sympathy with Mitya, of whom Alyosha, as Ivan knew, was very fond.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: He even succeeded in insulting Ivan during their first interview, telling him sharply that it was not for people who declared that “everything was lawful,” to suspect and question him.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: He used violent language, accused Smerdyakov, and was fearfully muddled.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: He put that off till he had seen Smerdyakov, who was at that time in the hospital.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: foreseeing such a calamity you deserted your own father, and would not protect us, for I might have been taken up any time for stealing that three thousand.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: Do you remember when Dmitri burst in after dinner and beat father, and afterwards I told you in the yard that I reserved ‘the right to desire’?

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: Do you remember when Dmitri burst in after dinner and beat father, and afterwards I told you in the yard that I reserved ‘the right to desire’?

triples.subject: Alyosha
triples.quote: Alyosha turned rather pale, and looked silently into his brother’s face.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: His chief feeling was one of relief at the fact that it was not Smerdyakov, but Mitya, who had committed the murder, though he might have been expected to feel the opposite.

triples.subject: Smerdyakov
triples.quote: My brother directly accuses you of the murder and theft.

triples.subject: Ivan
triples.quote: On his return from Moscow, he abandoned himself hopelessly to his mad and consuming passion for Katerina Ivanovna.

triples.subject: Katerina Ivanovna
triples.quote: did not abandon herself altogether to the man she loved, in spite of the Karamazov violence of his passions and the great fascination he had for her.

triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: Grigory’s wife, Marfa, in answer to Ivan’s questions, declared that Smerdyakov had been lying all night the other side of the partition wall.
